formNote: The Shuowen: 名，自命也。从口从夕。夕者，冥也。冥不相見，故以口自名 — “to name oneself… evening is dark; in the dark people cannot see each other, so they name themselves aloud.” A memorable Han explanation, not necessarily the graph’s origin.
summary: A name, and the act of naming. 名 runs from the Daodejing’s opening line (名可名，非常名) through Confucius’s call to rectify names, to the Buddhist 假名: the provisional names by which empty things are spoken of.
placement: Low at the front of the sphere, just above and to the left of 空, so that 假名 ("provisional name") is one short step from emptiness. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: Matches Wiktionary’s B–S basic-vocabulary list (v1.1, Sagart & Ma 2020), “name”; not yet checked against B–S 2014 itself.

satellites.title: Rectifying Names
satellites.evidence: Analects 13.3: 名不正，則言不順；言不順，則事不成 — “if names are not correct, speech does not accord with things; if speech does not accord, affairs do not succeed.” For Confucius, order begins with calling things what they are.

satellites.title: The Name Is the Guest of Reality
satellites.evidence: Zhuangzi ch. 1: declining the throne, Xu You says 名者，實之賓也 — “a name is the guest of reality.” The pair 名 / 實 (name and actuality) runs through early Chinese philosophy, and 實 is half of Rushi’s own name, 如實.

satellites.title: Name-and-Form
satellites.evidence: In the twelve links, nāma-rūpa, “name and form”, the mental and physical sides of a person, is rendered part for part as 名色: 名 for nāma, 色 for rūpa.
